text:
alex_customer: Hey team — streaming sessions from our Private VPC to Redwood stop delivering tokens after ~30s of silence. Client reports ECONNRESET or the socket just hangs until we reconnect. Affects prod and staging. Any quick triage steps?
maria_support: Sorry about that — can you confirm this is a Private deployment (VPC) and which region? Also any inline TLS inspection or customer NGFW?
alex_customer: Private (customer-managed VPC), us-west-2. Customer SRE says Palo Alto inline TLS-inspection is enabled. Repro steps: 1) open websocket to wss://api.redwood.internal/v1/streams 2) send prompt, receive partial stream 3) stop writing for ~30s 4) send more input -> client either sees nothing or gets ECONNRESET. No server errors in our app logs.
sam_network: Middleboxes with TLS rewrap or HTTP buffering will often hold chunks until they see a content-length/connection close or a TLS close_notify. TLS inspection can coalesce chunks and break streaming. NAT idle timeouts also silently drop state.

alex_customer: We captured tcpdump on our gateway. We see keepalive probes from the client, but the server keeps sending payloads that never arrive. No FINs on our side. Looks like packets get dropped or buffered mid-proxy.
maria_support: Two quick things to try: 1) ask the network team to bypass TLS inspection for api.redwood.internal (SNI bypass), 2) enable websocket-level pings from client every 15s. Both should reduce buffering/idle close.
jay_infra: On our side we can also enable an experimental keepalive chunk for your org: when streaming and no tokens emitted for >10s we send a 1-byte keepalive chunk (a single space) to keep middleboxes from idling. We rolled this to a staging host for org 12345 — monitor it.
alex_customer: Appreciate that. Any packet-level signs to look for in the pcap? We saw a TCP retransmit series right before the silence window.
sam_network: Look for TLS handshake messages that indicate renegotiation / rewrap (ClientHello after session established) and for repeated ACKs without payload. Middlebox buffer releases often coincide with a TLS rewrap or HTTP proxy completing a buffered chunk.
maria_support: Also confirm egress allowlist contains our public NAT IP ranges. If TLS is rewrapped, the proxy may present a different cert chain — check if clients report cert subject changes or SNI mismatch.
alex_customer: Quick client-side mitigation we added: websocket ping every 12s and application-level noop every 20s: ws.send(JSON.stringify({type:'noop'})). That reduced incidence but didn't fully eliminate it when TLS inspection is on.
jay_infra: Long-term options: increase firewall/NAT idle timers on the customer side, disable TLS inspection for streaming endpoints, or leave server keepalives enabled. We can recommend TCP keepalive intervals: TCP_KEEPCNT=5, TCP_KEEPINTVL=15, TCP_KEEPIDLE=30.
alex_customer: Repro note for internal engineers — minimal repro using wscat: wscat -c "wss://api.redwood.internal/v1/streams" then send a small prompt, wait 30s, then send another message. Attach pcap to the ticket — shows TLS ClientHello at ~30s.
maria_support: We'll keep the temporary 1-byte keepalive for your org on staging. If bypassing TLS inspection removes the issue, that confirms the middlebox. Please share the pcap link and we can coordinate with your SRE for firewall timer changes.
deploy-bot: rolled:stream-keepalive/org-12345 -> staging at 2026-03-17T12:08:32Z :rocket:
alex_customer: Thanks all — we'll try bypassing TLS inspection and report back. If that helps we'll work with our security team to add an SNI bypass for api.redwood.internal and increase NAT idle timers.
